key_facts: Council Bill 1089 proposes extending the minimum affordability period for affordable housing projects from 20 to 60 years.
The amendment to Council Bill 1089 delays the effective date of the 60-year affordability period to February 1st, 2019, allowing time for stakeholder input and rulemaking.
There are approximately 20,000 affordable housing units in Denver's portfolio, with over 5,000 funded by the city.
About 2,000 units in the city's portfolio are at risk of expiring over the next five years.
Councilwoman Kennish moved to delay the final consideration of Council Bill 1089 until February 19, 2019, which was seconded but ultimately failed.
Council Bill 975, which involves amendments to the inclusionary housing ordinance, was ordered published after a vote.
The council adjourned the meeting with several required public hearings scheduled for upcoming dates.
